claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC dendritic refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain at lower temperatures.
At 1273 K, unmodified TiVNbTa has approximately 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength.
A small, well-dispersed addition of nanoscale Y2O3 or another refractory oxide can be incorporated into TiVNbTa during processing.
The intervention will produce ultrafine, stable oxide precipitates uniformly distributed within the BCC matrix.
Nanoscale oxide particles will impede dislocation motion in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
Nanoscale oxide particles will retard grain-boundary sliding in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and retarded grain-boundary sliding will mitigate high-temperature softening.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve the high-temperature creep resistance of TiVNbTa.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have greater yield and compressive strength at 1273 K than unmodified TiVNbTa.
The oxide-dispersed alloy may attain a yield strength well above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The oxide-dispersed alloy can preserve acceptable ductility at 1273 K.
The oxide-dispersed alloy can preserve thermal conduction suitable for use as a heat-transfer interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
Keeping the oxide content sufficiently low will avoid deleterious secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The proposed mediator is a dispersion of oxide precipitates, which constitutes a second phase, while the boundary requires that the intervention not disrupt the single-phase BCC structure. This is internally inconsistent unless 'single-phase BCC' is explicitly limited to the metallic matrix rather than the entire material.
